case_title: OMA @ OMPRAKASH AND ANR. v. STATE OF TAMIL NADU
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction, modified sentence to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused and nine other individuals entered the house of a woman at night with the intention of committing burglary. During the burglary, they killed the husband of the woman by strangulation with a rope and assaulted the woman, her son, and another individual with iron rods. The accused were apprehended after ten years in connection with another case. An identification parade was conducted for one accused but not for the other. The iron rod used in the crime was recovered after ten years, but the prosecution could not establish a clear connection between the recovered rod and the crime. The trial court convicted both accused under sections 395, 396, and 397 of the IPC and sentenced them to death. The High Court confirmed the conviction but modified the sentence to life imprisonment. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction of the second accused due to insufficient evidence and the failure to properly identify him. The first accused died during the appeal, leading to the dismissal of his case.
